Police arrested 43 people after clashes and injuries at a March match.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Celtic and Rangers are contesting closed doors sanctions imposed following fan disorder during a match in March. Police Scotland arrested 43 people after fans clashed, injuring officers and stewards. An independent review found a crushing risk existed due to fans surging past security. Both clubs admitted to the original Scottish FA charges.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Celtic criticised the punishment as disproportionate for a small incursion during a moment of celebration. The club argued that, as the away team, they were not responsible for stadium safety arrangements. Meanwhile, an agreement has already been reached to ban away fans from all Old Firm derbies this season.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Derek McInnes began his tenure at Rangers with inconsistent results, including an early exit from European competitions. Despite initial criticism from fans, the team improved significantly throughout September, securing several consecutive wins and moving up the league table.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The recent turnaround has helped the club recover from a period of instability. By defeating Celtic twice, the squad has demonstrated progress and built a sense of unity that was previously lacking.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Rangers now look to maintain their momentum in the Scottish Premiership and prepare for a cup semi-final match against Aberdeen at Hampden.
